# CPython 3.13 Free Threading and Extension Imports

CPython 3.13 introduced experimental free threading as a configuration in which the Global Interpreter Lock (GIL) can be disabled. What happens next depends in part on the extensions an application imports.

If an extension has no explicit declaration of support for this mode, importing it produces a warning and enables the GIL. The declaration mechanism differs between extensions that use multi-phase initialization and those that use single-phase initialization.

Declaring support signals compatibility with the free-threading runtime mode; it does not establish that the extension’s code is thread-safe. Extension authors have a separate responsibility to make their code safe for threaded use.
